summary: Researchers from Donghu Laboratory in Hubei Province, China, have accelerated a 1.1-ton maglev vehicle to 650 km/h in seven seconds, setting a new world record for the fastest maglev train. title: China makes progress in power generation, storage on Mars
summary: Scientists from the University of Science and Technology of China have developed a special battery that uses Mars' CO2-rich atmosphere to generate and store energy, addressing a major challenge in Mars exploration. This self-fueling battery can power rovers and living quarters, reducing the battery system's weight and enabling in-situ energy acquisition. The development supports China's accelerated Mars exploration efforts, with the Tianwen-3 probe set to launch in 2028 and return samples to Earth by 2031.

title: China-World Robot Soccer League: Training Underway For Beijing Finale
summary: The RoBoLeague World Robot Soccer League will hold its final competition in Beijing, featuring autonomous humanoid robots in a 3-on-3 football match. This event serves as the first test for the upcoming World Humanoid Robot Games. The competition will take place in the Yizhuang Development Zone, with four Chinese teams qualifying for the finals. Teams from Tsinghua University and Beijing Information Science and Technology University demonstrated their robots' skills in a pre-competition training session. Each team consists of three players and one substitute, with matches comprising two 10-minute halves and a 5-minute break. The robots operate without human control, showcasing their ability to kick, run, and maneuver on the pitch. Dou Jing, an organizer, highlighted the event as a test of the robots' endurance and agility. Wang Yonghao, responsible for the competition's operations, noted that the robots are equipped with sensors for nimble movement, and rules specify the use of colors to minimize disturbances.

title: Pentagon denies leaked intel saying US strikes only delayed Iran's nuclear program
summary: A leaked intelligence report suggests that US airstrikes on Iran’s nuclear sites may have only delayed, not destroyed, its nuclear program. The operation on June 21, involving 125 aircraft and 14 bunker-busting bombs, was the largest B-2 bomber mission in history. However, insiders claim Iran had moved much of its enriched uranium beforehand and key equipment wasn’t destroyed. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth denied these claims, stating he had seen no intelligence indicating the targets were empty. The White House criticized the leak, calling it incorrect and blaming an individual for attempting to embarrass President Trump. The Pentagon presented footage of a bunker-buster strike, asserting its precision and effectiveness, with Trump describing it as a highly successful military strike. Some speculate the delayed briefing is related to the leak, but military officials deny any political pressure to alter the intelligence narrative. Iran’s Foreign Ministry stated its nuclear facilities were significantly impacted by recent US-Israeli airstrikes, though no specifics were provided.
